name: codemd-graphs
description: The auto test harness for AI-written code. CODEMD traces your callgraph to find exactly what changed, instantly re-runs the existing tests that cover it, and has Claude write the ones you're missing — one click, always under your control.

codemdGraphs.autoWriteProjectMcpConfig.deprecationMessage: CODEMD no longer writes MCP configuration automatically. Use the CODEMD: Add CODEMD MCP Server command or the Add CODEMD MCP Server button when you want to create/update MCP config.
codemdGraphs.autoWriteProjectMcpConfig.description: Deprecated. MCP setup is user-triggered only through the CODEMD: Add CODEMD MCP Server command or panel button.

codemdGraphs.autoReveal.description: Automatically open the CODEMD panel when a workspace loads, so the callgraph appears without needing to click the CODEMD activity bar icon first.

codemdGraphs.backendDir.description: Path to the folder containing the CODEMD analyzer backend (main.py). Leave empty to use the backend bundled with this extension. If no bundled backend is available, Generate CODEMD will prompt for an explicit backend folder.

codemdGraphs.pythonPath.description: Python executable used to launch the local FastAPI server. Leave unset (default) to have the extension auto-create and manage an isolated virtual environment with the required dependencies in global storage. Set this explicitly to use a specific interpreter instead — in that case it must already have backend/requirements.txt installed.

codemdGraphs.analysisMode.description: How Generate CODEMD runs local analysis. Use cli for the default local subprocess path; use server to force the FastAPI workflow.

codemdGraphs.host.description: Host the local FastAPI server binds to.

codemdGraphs.port.description: Port the local FastAPI server binds to.

codemdGraphs.readOnlyMode.description: When enabled, CODEMD never invokes Claude to write tests or fix failures — it only analyzes, and runs tests that already exist. The free, mechanical Regression Test (no AI involved) is unaffected.

codemdGraphs.maxCostPerActionUsd.description: Caps how much API-equivalent usage a single Claude action (writing a test, fixing a failure, or finding how to run a test) can use, in USD. On a Claude Pro/Max subscription this isn't a real charge — it's the same usage figure the CLI reports internally — but the cap still protects your rate-limited 5-hour/7-day quota from one runaway action. Claude stops as soon as it crosses this between turns and the action is reported as failed rather than applied; since the check happens between turns, not mid-turn, actual usage can run slightly over this for one expensive turn. Raise it if you want to allow heavier actions.

codemdGraphs.runMode.description: Whether the panel checks and runs existing tests for a changed function automatically (Auto, the default — pure local pytest, no Claude call) or only when you click Check existing tests (Manual). Forced to auto whenever codemdGraphs.writeMode is auto, since auto-write relies on this check's result.

codemdGraphs.writeMode.description: Whether the panel invokes Claude to write New-Function/Contract/Broad-Coverage tests automatically as changed functions are found (Auto) or only when you click their chip (Manual, the default). Auto spends real Claude usage without a click each time, capped by codemdGraphs.maxAutoWritesPerBatch and codemdGraphs.maxCostPerActionUsd; has no effect while codemdGraphs.readOnlyMode is on.

codemdGraphs.maxAutoWritesPerBatch.description: Caps how many tests codemdGraphs.writeMode: auto will generate within one Check Uncommitted Changes / Check Latest Commits / Analyze Commit result set. Functions beyond the cap keep their normal manual chip instead of auto-firing, so one large commit can't silently trigger a wall of Claude calls.

codemdGraphs.excludeGlobs.description: Additional glob patterns to exclude when zipping the workspace for analysis, on top of the built-in defaults (.git, node_modules, venvs, build output).
